- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 2 (units? probably grams, but not stated; e ≥ 2, keep value {min:2, max:null}, unit null... Hmm. e ≥ 2 — in weighing, e would be in g. But not stated. I'll leave unit null or "g"? Not stated — don't fabricate. Keep unit null.)
- Weighing range(s): Multi-interval (string value)
- Maximum number of scale intervals (multi-interval): n ≤ 3000 (per partial weighing range) → {min:null, max:3000}, footnote? "(per partial weighing range)" is a note but not a numbered footnote. I could put it in description... The schema values have footnote_markers for numbered footnotes. The "(per partial weighing range)" qualifier — maybe include as part of the attribute label: maximum_number_of_scale_intervals_per_partial_range? Or keep attribute "maximum_number_of_scale_intervals_multi_interval" with value {min:null, max:3000}. I'll keep it simple.
- Maximum number of partial weighing ranges: 2
- Tare: T ≤ -Max₁ - e₁ for multi-interval instruments → formula string: "T <= -Max1 - e1" — keep as string value. Attribute: tare. Value: "T ≤ -Max₁ - e₁" — should avoid LaTeX but this is plain unicode, fine. Maybe "T ≤ −Max1 − e1 for multi-interval instruments". Keep the condition separate? I could write value: "T ≤ -Max₁ - e₁". Hmm, subscript unicode. Let me write "T ≤ -Max1 - e1".
- Temperature range: 0 °C / +40 °C → {min:0, max:40}, unit °C
- Power supply voltage: 24 V DC supplied by 100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz adapter → split:
  - instrument_supply_voltage: 24 V DC
  - adapter_input_voltage: 100-240 V AC
  - adapter_input_frequency: 50-60 Hz
  - power_supply_type: "DC (via AC adapter)" or "DC"
- Application: direct sales to the public → string
- Software identification:
  - Main version number: V2.1.2 (string)
  - Checksum: 1489017833 (string? it's numeric but an identifier — keep as string to avoid losing leading info; but rules say numbers not strings... it's an identifier, not a measurement. I'll keep as string "1489017833". Actually could be number. Safer as string since it's an identifier.)
  - AD board version: V1.121 (string)
  - Checksum: FF42432F (string)

Model family: The remark says all instrument types have the same hardware and software; load cell capacity and housing colour can differ. The type list has 25 model names. The pairs: AURORA Y1 = iMachine E1? Looking at layout: "AURORA Y1 — AURORA Y1 Pro — iMachine E1" — each row seems to be three designations, possibly the same instrument sold under different names. Rows: 8 rows of 3 + iMachine E9 = 25 designations.

Should I create model_family? The types differ but characteristics are the same (same hardware/software). The cert covers multiple type designations. Per schema, model_family "include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". The cert covers 25 type designations. But they all share the same characteristics. Hmm — the matrix detection rule is about varying attributes per model. Here no attribute varies by model (Max range 6-30 kg applies to all). The remark says load cell capacity and housing color can differ.

I think I should list all type designations in certified_type.type_designations, and optionally a model_family with these 25 models. Since attributes don't vary per model, model_level would be empty. The schema says model_family include only if >1 model variant. There are >1 designations, so include with family names? There's no explicit family name... could say "AURORA / iMachine". Hmm, don't fabricate — family_name null. But listing 25 models with model_id seems reasonable. Actually, the pairs might be equivalent names: e.g., AURORA Y1, AURORA Y1 Pro, and iMachine E1 might be the same instrument under different brands. But I can't be sure. I'll list all 25 as models.

Actually let me reconsider: the remark says "All instrument types mentioned have the same hardware and software. The load cell capacity and the colour of the housing can be different." So load cell capacity varies (which relates to Max range 6-30 kg). But no per-model table. So model_level is not extractable beyond what's given. I'll include model_family with all 25 model_ids, and no model_level attributes since nothing varies per model in the data given. Hmm, but is including model_family without model_level okay? Schema allows it.

Alternatively keep it simpler: type_designations list of 25, and model_family omitted. The rule 4 says "Many OIML certs cover a FAMILY of instrument models... Detect this and put varying attributes in model_level, NOT type_level." Here there is no varying attribute table. I think including model_family with models is fine and informative. Let me include it.
